analyses.name: NVIDIA Corporation
analyses.verdict: A three-month base built on top of 85% revenue growth has compressed the multiple to 17.6x forward — the consolidation is the opportunity and the print in 13 days is the risk.

financials.summary: Datacenter is effectively the entire company now, dwarfing gaming, professional visualisation and automotive combined. The Blackwell generation carried the year with supply, not demand, as the binding constraint throughout. Gross margin held in the mid-70s despite a mix shift toward complete rack-scale systems, which carry more bought-in content than merchant silicon does — that margin defence is the single most impressive line in the statements. Operating leverage was extreme: earnings grew roughly two and a half times faster than revenue. Free cash flow was large enough to fund aggressive buybacks alongside the capital commitments behind the announced domestic build programme, and the balance sheet remains net-cash, which matters a great deal in a cycle where much of the AI complex is financing capacity with debt.
highlights: Revenue +85.2% year over year
EPS +214.5% — operating leverage running far ahead of the top line
Datacenter is the overwhelming majority of revenue; gaming is now a rounding error by comparison
Gross margin sustained in the mid-70s through the rack-scale mix shift
Networking (NVLink, InfiniBand, Ethernet) has grown into a material second business rather than an accessory
Net-cash balance sheet funding capacity commitments without leverage
Forward P/E of 17.6x — a market multiple for the fastest-growing mega-cap in the scan

accomplishments: Blackwell ramped to volume production and became the default training platform for frontier model builders
Moved from component supplier to infrastructure principal with a multi-hundred-billion domestic AI build commitment
Extended the CUDA software moat — switching cost, not silicon, remains the durable advantage
Reached roughly $5.46T market capitalisation, the largest company in the scanned universe
Grew networking into a standalone franchise, capturing more of the rack's value

journey_52w.summary: A year of two distinct halves. The first was a powerful advance as Blackwell shipped and hyperscaler capex guidance ratcheted higher through every reporting cycle. The second has been a three-month consolidation — three-month momentum is actually -4.3% — as the market digested both the size of the capacity commitments and the credit implications of an industry funding buildout with debt. Price now sits at 225.30, 4.3% below the 235.47 high, having ranged from 164.98 to 235.47 across the year. The critical detail is that earnings compounded through the entire flat stretch, which is what turned a rich multiple into a reasonable one without the stock falling. Six VCP contractions tightening to 2.9% describe a base under accumulation, not distribution — though volume at 0.80x average says the accumulation is patient rather than urgent.

analyses.name: U.S. Bancorp
analyses.verdict: At its 52-week high with a 2.6% tight base, 11.3x forward earnings and full TradingView agreement — the cleanest risk-reward on the board, held back only by thin volume.

financials.summary: A textbook regional-bank recovery year. Net interest income stabilised as deposit costs peaked and the securities book repriced into higher yields, while fee income from payments and trust services grew steadily and provides the diversification that pure spread lenders lack. Credit costs stayed contained — commercial real estate remained the watched exposure but did not produce the losses the bears modelled. Expense discipline turned modest revenue growth into meaningfully faster earnings growth, and capital ratios rebuilt to the point where buybacks resumed as a genuine use of capital rather than a token gesture.

EPS +21.6% — expense discipline amplifying revenue growth
Forward P/E of 11.3x, a discount to the money-centre banks
Payments and trust fee income diversifying away from pure spread revenue
Credit costs contained despite persistent commercial real estate concerns
Capital ratios rebuilt sufficiently to support sustained buybacks

analyses.name: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
analyses.verdict: The only large leader where price and relative strength are BOTH at new highs on above-average volume, at 8.5x forward earnings — mutual confirmation you rarely get this cheap.

financials.summary: A powerful year for life and health reinsurance. Mortality experience normalised toward pricing assumptions after several distorted years, which alone produced a large swing in reported earnings — this is the main reason EPS growth prints at 159.6% and it is important to understand it as normalisation rather than a new run rate. Underneath that, the business genuinely grew: premium volumes expanded as primary insurers ceded more risk, and pension risk transfer and longevity transactions added large block deals. The investment portfolio benefited from reinvesting at higher yields, which flows straight to the bottom line in a spread-based business. Book value per share compounded well.

EPS +159.6% — largely mortality normalisation, not a repeatable growth rate

analyses.name: Ross Stores, Inc.
analyses.verdict: Highest combined score in the entire 451-name universe, but TradingView says NEUTRAL and earnings land in 7 days — a genuine disagreement worth sizing around rather than ignoring.

financials.summary: Off-price retail executed while full-price retail struggled. Comparable store sales grew on higher transaction counts rather than ticket inflation, which is the healthier of the two drivers and indicates genuine share gain rather than pricing. Merchandise margin expanded as buying opportunities improved — when full-price retailers over-order, the off-price channel gets better goods at better prices, and that is exactly the environment that persisted. Distribution and freight costs, which had been a multi-year headwind, moderated. Store expansion continued at a measured pace, and the combination of margin expansion and share count reduction produced EPS growth nearly double the revenue growth rate.

analyses.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
analyses.verdict: The purest expression of the live Hormuz supply shock at 10.8x forward earnings — a real catalyst with a real reversal trigger, extended enough that entries need discipline.

financials.summary: A refining-margin year of the sort that produces numbers like these. Crack spreads widened materially as global refining capacity stayed tight against firm product demand, and Marathon's scale and complexity meant it captured a disproportionate share of that widening — complex refineries earn the most when the spread between heavy crude input and light product output is at its widest. Throughput ran high with strong utilisation across the system. The midstream segment provided a fee-based earnings floor that partially offset refining's inherent volatility. Cash generation was enormous and went overwhelmingly to buybacks, meaningfully shrinking the share count and amplifying per-share earnings growth on top of the operating result.

The macro driver is not subtle: overnight the US threatened an indefinite blockade of Iran, Hormuz shipping traffic is capped amid competing US and Iranian claims, and refined-product flows are rerouting — fuel oil from Malaysia's PRefChem refinery is heading to the US for the first time since 2023, which is exactly what a dislocated product market looks like. That is genuine, observable tightness rather than a narrative. The corresponding truth is that price now sits 25% above the 50-day at 286.01 with RSI 71.3, so the stock has already discounted a great deal of it.

analyses.name: Expeditors International of Washington, Inc.
analyses.verdict: Price and relative strength both at new highs with a 2.4% tight contraction, +32% revenue growth and TradingView STRONG BUY at 17 buy / 0 sell — the highest-quality industrial setup on the board.

financials.summary: An asset-light freight forwarder in a favourable rate environment, which is where the operating leverage in this model shows up. Revenue grew 32.1% as air and ocean freight rates firmed and volumes held, while net revenue — the spread the company actually earns between what it charges shippers and what it pays carriers — expanded faster than gross revenue. Because Expeditors owns no ships or planes, that spread expansion drops almost entirely to operating income, producing EPS growth well ahead of the top line. The company carries no meaningful debt and holds substantial net cash, which is why it can trade through freight downturns without the balance-sheet stress that asset-heavy carriers face. Cash returns continued through buybacks.

analyses.name: FedEx Corporation
analyses.verdict: The only leader on the board with genuinely convincing volume — 1.58x average at the 52-week high — but revenue is recovering faster than profit, and EPS is still negative.

financials.summary: A transition year where the top line turned before the bottom line did. Revenue grew 12.5% as volumes recovered across both Express and Ground and yields firmed, but EPS still declined 4.3% — the cost structure has not yet caught up with the revenue recovery. The multi-year network consolidation programme, combining the separate Express and Ground operations into a single integrated network, continued to absorb cash and management attention, with the savings arriving later than the disruption. International Express remained the weakest segment as trade-lane mix shifted. The honest read is that this is a self-help story where the self-help is still in progress: the market is paying for the revenue inflection and the eventual cost outcome, not for current profitability.

analyses.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
analyses.verdict: What AI infrastructure demand looks like once it reaches the income statement — revenue +87.5%, EPS +282.5%, at the 52-week high on 1.33x volume, with a high-bar print in 21 days.

financials.summary: The AI server cycle arrived in the reported numbers with force. Infrastructure Solutions carried the year as AI-optimised server shipments scaled from a promising backlog into large recognised revenue, nearly doubling total company revenue. The critical nuance is margin: AI servers carry substantially thinner gross margins than traditional enterprise infrastructure because so much of the bill of materials is bought-in accelerator content. Dell managed the mix well enough that operating income still grew several times faster than revenue, but the margin percentage tells a different story than the dollar growth does. The client PC business remained the stable, cash-generative counterweight. Backlog and deferred revenue both built through the year, which is the forward-looking indicator that matters most here.

analyses.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
analyses.verdict: 6.1x forward earnings against +345.7% revenue growth is the most extreme valuation-versus-growth gap in the scan — the market is pricing a cycle top, and it might be right.

financials.summary: A memory upcycle of historic proportions. DRAM and NAND contract pricing rose sharply as AI accelerator demand consumed high-bandwidth memory capacity that could not be added quickly, and because memory is a commodity with enormous operating leverage, revenue growth of 345.7% translated into EPS growth of 1368.5%. HBM was the story within the story: allocation sold out well into the following year at prices and margins far above commodity DRAM. Capital expenditure rose substantially to add capacity, which is both the rational response and the seed of the next downcycle. Gross margin expanded to levels that are historically unsustainable — memory margins always mean-revert, the only question is when.
highlights: Revenue +345.7% year over year on DRAM and NAND contract pricing
EPS +1368.5% — the extreme operating leverage inherent to commodity memory
HBM allocation sold out well into the following year at premium margins
Gross margin expanded to historically high, historically unsustainable levels
Capital expenditure rose sharply to add capacity — rational now, risk later
Forward P/E of 6.1x, the lowest among all leaders in the scan

accomplishments: Secured major HBM supply agreements with AI accelerator makers, sold out well forward
Executed the technology node transitions needed to compete at the leading edge of HBM
Converted the pricing upcycle into balance-sheet repair, moving from a leveraged to a strong net position
Expanded domestic manufacturing capacity with government incentive support

journey_52w.summary: From 115.60 to a high of 1213.37 — a move of roughly ten times — followed by a 21.7% drawdown to the current 949.83. That drawdown is the entire analytical question. Six VCP contractions tightening to 3.6% suggest the pullback has been orderly rather than a rout, but price is trading just BELOW the 50-day at 962.81 and relative strength is 26% off its high, so the leadership has clearly left the memory group for the moment. TradingView still rates it BUY on 14 buy signals against 2 sells. The 6.1x forward multiple is not the market handing out a bargain — it is the market explicitly pricing the belief that these earnings are a cycle peak that will not repeat. Whether that belief is right is the trade.

analyses.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited
analyses.verdict: The chokepoint for every AI accelerator sold, at 19.8x forward with +77% EPS growth — the permanent Taiwan discount is exactly why the multiple stays this reasonable.

financials.summary: The foundry monopoly at the leading edge, monetised. Revenue grew 36.0% as advanced-node capacity ran effectively sold out, with high-performance computing and AI accelerator customers displacing smartphone as the largest revenue contributor. EPS grew 77.4%, well ahead of revenue, because leading-edge nodes carry the highest margins in the industry and utilisation was near capacity — in foundry, incremental wafer volume on a depreciated node is enormously profitable. Pricing power was evident: the company has been able to raise advanced-node wafer prices, something only a supplier with no real alternative can do. Capital expenditure remained very large, funding both leading-edge capacity and geographic diversification into the US, Japan and Europe, which carries a structurally higher cost base than Taiwan fabs.
highlights: Revenue +36.0% year over year on sold-out advanced-node capacity
EPS +77.4% — leading-edge margin plus near-full utilisation
High-performance computing and AI displaced smartphone as the largest revenue segment
Demonstrated advanced-node pricing power, raising wafer prices without losing volume
Large capex funding both leading-edge nodes and geographic diversification
Forward P/E of 19.8x for an effective monopoly at the leading edge

accomplishments: Maintained an effective monopoly on leading-edge logic manufacturing with no credible competitor at the node
Ramped overseas fabs in the US and Japan, reducing single-jurisdiction concentration
Raised advanced-node wafer pricing — the clearest possible demonstration of pricing power
Grew advanced packaging capacity, the bottleneck that gates AI accelerator supply

journey_52w.summary: From 224.84 to a high of 477.57 and now 430.49 — a 91% advance from the low with a 9.9% pullback from the high, sitting right on the 50-day at 425.25. That precise positioning is what makes the current setup attractive: the stop is close and the invalidation is unambiguous. There is no clear VCP here, so the base is less orderly than the other technology leaders, and volume at 0.61x with relative strength 13% off its high both say participation has cooled. TradingView rates it BUY on 16 buy signals against 3 sells. The year's dominant non-fundamental factor remains geopolitical: China called Taiwan's annual military drills a 'wasteful charade' overnight, and that steady drumbeat is the reason a monopoly with 77% EPS growth trades at 19.8x rather than 30x.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: Revenue +47.7% at a $1.08T market cap is the most improbable statistic in the scan, and RSI 52.2 just 2% below the high means you are not paying up for momentum.

financials.summary: Incretin therapies redefined the scale of what a pharmaceutical franchise can be. Revenue grew 47.7% — a growth rate that would be notable for a mid-cap and is close to unprecedented at trillion-dollar scale — driven overwhelmingly by GLP-1 receptor agonists across both diabetes and obesity indications. The binding constraint all year was manufacturing capacity rather than prescription demand, and the company spent heavily to expand fill-finish and API capacity, which is the moat competitors cannot simply buy. EPS grew 26.2%, slower than revenue, because of that capacity investment and the substantial rebate and access spending required to secure payer coverage at scale. Gross margins remained very high, as they do for branded biologics.

GLP-1 franchise across both diabetes and obesity drove the overwhelming majority of growth

Forward P/E of 25.5x, defensible against a 47.7% revenue growth rate

analyses.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp.
analyses.verdict: NEW LISTING — judge the business, not the quant signals: a genuine launch and broadband monopoly at a $1.86T valuation that already prices near-flawless execution.

financials.period: FY2025 (first full fiscal year disclosed around the listing)
financials.summary: Two businesses inside one company, moving at different speeds. Launch is the mature side: reusable heavy-lift cadence far beyond any competitor, with both commercial and government customers, and economics that improve with every reflight because the marginal cost of a recovered booster is refurbishment rather than manufacture. Starlink is the growth side and is now the dominant revenue line — a consumer and enterprise broadband subscription business with satellite manufacturing vertically integrated, which is why the unit economics work where previous satellite broadband ventures failed. Revenue grew 91.9%. Profitability remains constrained by the capital intensity of both constellation replenishment and the Starship development programme; this is a business investing far ahead of its current revenue base, and the 76.3x forward multiple is the market underwriting that investment. Treat all figures here as public-disclosure level rather than a mature reporting history.
highlights: Revenue +91.9% year over year, with Starlink now the dominant contributor
Reusable heavy-lift launch cadence far ahead of any competitor
Vertically integrated satellite manufacturing underpins Starlink unit economics
Forward P/E of 76.3x at a $1.86T market capitalisation
Heavy ongoing capital intensity from constellation replenishment and Starship development
Limited reporting history — a first-year public issuer, so comparability is thin

accomplishments: Established the only high-cadence reusable heavy-lift launch capability at commercial scale
Scaled Starlink into a global consumer and enterprise broadband business with millions of subscribers
Advanced the Starship programme toward operational flights, which would reset launch cost per kilogram again
Completed one of the largest public listings on record, giving the equity a public market for the first time
Secured major government and defence launch and communications contracts

journey_52w.summary: A short and volatile public history. The stock listed into enormous demand, ran to 211.39, and has since given back a third of that to 141.29 — an entirely normal post-IPO pattern as the initial allocation froth is worked off and the float grows. It now trades just below its 50-day at 141.85, with relative strength 36% off its high and a 45.5 combined score that should be discounted heavily: quant signals built on 50-day and 52-week statistics are close to meaningless on a stock with this little trading history, which is precisely why this is framed as a business thesis rather than a technical one. TradingView shows BUY but on a thin sample of 9 buy, 5 sell and 5 neutral signals — no established rating exists for a new listing yet, and that is expected rather than a warning.

Size it as a long-duration position, not a trade.
